title: Hardening graph capture/replay for concurrent multi-stream decodes and kernel routing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Production decodes are intermittently failing when using CUDA graph capture + multi-stream decode paths. Failures manifest as replay errors (cudaGraphLaunch returning errors) or silent correctness regressions for some tokens when high-concurrency prefill+decode workloads exercise mixed kernel sets (FlashAttention, custom fused attention kernels, and fallback cuBLAS matmuls). This ticket centralizes engineering work to make capture/replay robust across kernel selection changes and concurrent stream scheduling.
background: Root causes observed during on-call investigation: 1) Non-deterministic scheduler ordering between prefill captures and decode replays can cause graph instantiation that captures pointers/allocations tied to a different stream or temporary arena; 2) Kernel selector may swap to a different attention kernel at runtime based on sequence-length heuristics, invalidating previously captured graphs; 3) Some third-party kernels (optimized FlashAttention) use internal workspace allocations that are not stable across captures, causing replay-time memory-layout mismatches; 4) Multi-GPU mempool fragmentation during heavy concurrent runs leads to address differences between capture and replay.
design_notes: Principles: make capture idempotent, decouple kernel routing decisions from a single-capture lifetime, and provide safe fast-fail fallbacks. Proposed changes: - Introduce a capture-safety check that validates kernel set and allocator state before cudaGraphInstantiate; - Lock down kernel routing during capture by emitting a capture-compatible kernel signature (model config + seq len bucket + quantization profile) and bind to a stable code-path; - Use stream-affinity invariants: ensure instantiated graph is executed only on streams with identical pool/arena states or use stream-local mempools for captured graphs; - Add a lightweight capture-version tag to graph objects so replay verifies compatibility (kernel signatures + allocator epoch); - Heuristic to avoid capture for thin/short-lived sessions (where capture overhead outweighs benefit) or when allocator churn is high; - Add retry path: on replay error, fall back to immediate non-captured decode and schedule a graph re-capture with synced allocator state.
implementation_plan:
Tasks:
1) Kernel-signature layer (ENG-17909) - compute deterministic signature for chosen kernels and parameters; expose via runtime API.
2) Capture-safety validator (ENG-17910) - checks allocator epoch, kernel signature, and stream affinity prior to instantiate; return consistent error codes.
3) MemPool pinning and stream-local pools (ENG-17911) - implement optional stream-local arenas used during graph capture/replay.
4) Fallback plumbing - implement replay error handlers to switch to non-capture decode and trigger safe recapture.
5) Unit + stress tests - add fuzz harness that simulates interleaved captures and replays with different kernel sets and varying allocator conditions.
6) Instrumentation - add new metrics: graph_instantiate_failures, graph_replay_fallbacks, capture_signature_mismatch.
7) PR and rollout: incremental PRs for each task with feature flags to enable/disable safety checks.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge kernel-signature and validator behind feature flag. 2) Deploy runtime-1.20 canary with safety checks enabled for 10% of traffic (dedicated capacity only). 3) Monitor capture_instantiate_failures and latency. 4) Enable mempool pinning on canary hosts. 5) If stable after 48h, increase to 50% then full deploy. 6) Default enable for all Dedicated hosts in next patch release. 7) Provide escaped rollbacks to disable capture-path entirely if regressions appear.
test_plan: - Unit tests for signature equality across identical config runs. - Integration test: capture on stream A, replay on stream B with same pool -> should succeed. - Negative test: intentionally change kernel selection and assert capture-safety blocks instantiate. - Nightly stress job: run 6h concurrent prefill+decode with random seq lengths across GPUs to detect flakiness. - Fuzz: random allocator pressure with repeated capture/replay cycles to detect address mismatches. - Add correctness checks to token-level outputs for a fixed prompt suite to assert no regression after fixes.
acceptance_criteria: >= 90% reduction in graph_instantiate_failures on canary hosts compared to baseline
No silent token-level regressions observed across nightly correctness suite (0 diffs allowed)
Replay fallback path exercised and recorded without customer-visible errors during test runs
Instrumentation metrics added and dashboards exist: graph_instantiate_failures, graph_replay_fallbacks, capture_signature_mismatch
notes: Trade-offs: locking kernel selection reduces capture reuse when dynamic kernel heuristics would otherwise pick a faster kernel during replay. We'll mitigate by making signatures coarse-grained (seq-bucketed) and adding guided recapture for cases where a different kernel yields significantly better perf. This work touches allocator internals and requires careful QA on both Ampere and Hopper families; we will prioritize Hopper nodes in canaries because address-space layout differences surfaced most there.
